fullPassage: In order to efficiently process information, our brains employ strategies that affect how we gather and interpret data. One of these strategies is called confirmation bias, and it occurs when we interpret information in a way that supports what we already believe. A study from Stanford University in 1979 revealed how powerful confirmation bias is. Researchers produced two fake research reports with opposing arguments about the effects of capital punishment. One of the reports suggested that capital punishment leads to reduced crime rates, while the other proposed that the two were not related. When participants were presented with these fabricated reports, their responses were shown to be significantly influenced by their existing opinions on the issue. Even when they encountered evidence that contradicted their beliefs, the impact of confirmation bias proved to be highly significant.

det.korean: reveal(동사: 드러내다) → revealed(과거형: 드러냈다). 1979년이라는 과거 시점
det.analysis: reveal을 과거형 revealed로 변환. 'A study ... in 1979 revealed'—1979년에 일어난 일이므로 과거시제가 필요해요.
det.tip: 1979(과거 연도)가 단서 → 과거형 revealed

questions.passage: When participants were presented with these fabricated reports, their responses were shown to be significantly __________ (influence) by their existing opinions on the issue.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: influence(동사: 영향을 주다) → influenced(과거분사: 영향받은). be동사+p.p. 수동태
det.analysis: influence를 과거분사 influenced로 변환. 'to be significantly influenced by ~'—반응이 '영향을 받는' 것이므로 be+과거분사(수동태)가 필요해요. 뒤의 by가 수동태 신호예요.
det.tip: to be _____ by ~ → 수동태(be+과거분사) → influenced

questions.passage: In order to efficiently process information, our brains employ strategies that affect how we gather and interpret data. One of these strategies is called confirmation bias, and it occurs when we interpret information in a way that __________ what we already believe. A study from Stanford University in 1979 revealed how powerful confirmation bias is. Researchers produced two fake research reports with opposing arguments about the effects of capital punishment. One of the reports suggested that capital punishment leads to reduced crime rates, while the other proposed that the two were not related. When participants were presented with these fabricated reports, their responses were shown to be significantly influenced by their existing opinions on the issue. Even when they encountered evidence that contradicted their beliefs, the impact of confirmation bias proved to be highly significant.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: questions=의문을 제기하다 / denies=부인하다 / ignores=무시하다 / supports=뒷받침하다
det.analysis:
① questions: 이미 믿는 것에 의문을 제기하는 방식? 확증 편향과 반대
② denies: 부인하는 방식? 반대
③ ignores: 무시하는 방식? 반대
④ supports: 이미 믿는 것을 뒷받침하는 방식으로 해석 ←정답
det.tip: 확증 편향 = 이미 믿는 것을 supports(뒷받침하는) 방향으로 해석

questions.passage: In order to efficiently process information, our brains employ strategies that affect how we gather and interpret data. One of these strategies is called confirmation bias, and it occurs when we interpret information in a way that supports what we already believe. A study from Stanford University in 1979 revealed how powerful confirmation bias is. Researchers produced two fake research reports with opposing arguments about the effects of capital punishment. One of the reports suggested that capital punishment leads to reduced crime rates, while the other proposed that the two were not related. When participants were presented with these fabricated reports, their responses were shown to be significantly influenced by their existing __________ on the issue. Even when they encountered evidence that contradicted their beliefs, the impact of confirmation bias proved to be highly significant.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: facts=사실 / reports=보고서 / opinions=의견 / crimes=범죄
det.analysis:
① facts: 기존 사실에 영향받음? 사실은 편향의 대상이 아님
② reports: 기존 보고서? 문맥 부적절
③ opinions: 그 사안에 대한 기존 '의견'에 반응이 영향받음 ←정답
④ crimes: 기존 범죄? 문맥 부적절
det.tip: existing _____ on the issue(사안에 대한 기존 것) = opinions(의견)
